{#eqwh} # Discussion

{#pi1r} Our study indicated that silencing PinX1 enhances radiosensitivity and antitumor-immunity of RT by enhancing IR-induced telomere dysfunction, therefore improving the antitumor efficiency of radioimmunotherapy.

{#sose} PinX1 was initially identified as a telomerase-binding protein with a highly potent inhibitor of telomerase activity [@w:w27]. However, many studies have suggested that PinX1 positively regulates telomere maintenance and promotes genome stability in tumor cells [@w:w28]. The role of PinX1 in tumorigenesis and progression varies widely among cancer types [@w:w29]. For NSCLC, previous studies have shown that PinX1 inhibits tumor cell proliferation [@w:w30]. Our previous studies have shown that the high expression of PinX1 induced radioresistance through promoting telomere maintenance and chromosome stabilization, and targeting PinX1 significantly enhances radiosensitivity via increasing IR-induced telomere dysfunction in ESCC [@w:w31]. In the in vitro experimental part of our study (including colony formation assay and CCK-8 assay), knockdown of PinX1 also increased cell proliferation of tumor cells to a certain extent, however, when combined with RT, cell proliferation appeared significantly downregulated relative to RT alone. In the in vivo part of the experiment, our results showed that the tumor volume did not significantly increase in the sh

ops.markdown: Our study found that silencing PinX1 plus IR significantly increased CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell infiltration and CD8<sup>+</sup> cytotoxic T lymphocytes in tumor tissues and peripheral immune organs. CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell infiltration and activation correlate strongly with prognosis in several cancers [@w:w42], and their antitumor immunity has been suggested as a determinant of ICB effectiveness. Radiation promotes CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell infiltration by inducing DSBs that activate the cGAS-STING pathway and releases tumor-associated antigens and chemokines [@w:w43]. Indeed, silencing PinX1 markedly enhanced cGAS-STING pathway activation by increasing IR-induced free dsDNA production.

{#b09q} # Background

{#v1gs} Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for roughly 85% of all lung cancer cases and substantially contributes to cancer deaths worldwide . Both immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) immunotherapy and radiotherapy are first-line treatments for NSCLC. For locally advanced NSCLC, chemoradiation combined with ICB has become the standard treatment. [@w:w1] However, the curative efficacy of radio-immunotherapy is still suboptimal, and radioresistance remains a significant barrier to improving the antitumor-immunity of IR, limiting the survival benefit of NSCLC from radiotherapy–immunotherapy combinations [@w:w2].
